equity_bridge.note: Senior to common; deducted at carrying value at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet) rather than charging the ~$265M/yr preferred dividend to the flows - the more conservative of the two at a 10.25% cost of equity (265 / 0.1025 = 2,585 < 4,055). Was 3,559: Series L ($496M net, August 2026) proved incremental, Series G was not redeemed.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2031 average revenue growth (4.5-5.0%); equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because STT returns ~80% of earnings and swapped $1.5B of preferred out in FY2024, which mechanically suppresses book growth without describing earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 1.2% vs revenue 3.6% and EPS 8.3% - divergence >30%. Cause is distribution policy (diluted share count cut from 357.1M FY2020 to 289.0M FY2025, -19%) and AOCI swings, not a deteriorating franchise. EPS CAGRs are buyback-flattered: net income grew only 4.0%/yr over the same five years.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are computed on NET INCOME (the FCFE proxy: FY2025 2,945 vs FY2022 2,774 vs FY2020 2,420), not on the CSV's reported FCF, which is deposit-flow noise for a custody bank (FY2024 -14,136, FY2025 +10,843). Revenue: FY2025 13,944 / FY2022 12,148 / FY2020 11,703. EPS (CSV, basic): 9.55 / 7.28 / 6.40. Equity (total, incl. preferred): 27,841 / 25,191 / 26,200. FY2025 net income is depressed by $326M restructuring; ex that, the 5-yr NI CAGR is ~5.5%. FY2026E is a step-change year (+13% revenue, record markets) that the CAGRs do not yet contain.

scenario_narratives.base: State Street's value turns on four axes: (1) servicing-fee growth on a record $59.2T of AUC/A, which the base case holds at mid-single digits as ~$400B/quarter of new mandates are won ($429B in Q3-2026, $2.98T still to be installed) and markets compound, against persistent custody fee compression; (2) SSGA/SPDR management fees on $6.3T AUM, which ride ETF adoption but are market-level sensitive; (3) net interest income (~21% of revenue), which gives back part of 2026's +14-15% as the Fed eases; and (4) operating leverage from the $1B transformation programme, which lifts the pretax margin from FY2026's ~32.8% to 33.5% - most of management's ~35% medium-term target, discounted for STT's history of never sustaining much above 30%. Revenue grows 4.5-5% to FY2031 and 3% thereafter; FY2027 is modelled soft (+4.5%, ~80bps margin give-back to 32.0%) because 2026 was lifted by record markets and trading volumes management itself does not extrapolate. ~85% of earnings is modelled as distributed (9M-2026 actual: 71%) through the $0.92 quarterly dividend and buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Equity markets keep compounding and the mandate pipeline converts: fee revenue grows high-single-digit for two more years, State Street Alpha and the Latam securities-services acquisition add genuine new revenue lines, and the 2026 operating-leverage run-rate persists so the 35% pretax target is hit by FY2029 and slightly exceeded. Capital-light fee growth (0.7x retention) lets payout stay ~85-90%. Digital-asset/tokenisation custody optionality is NOT separately priced - it is upside to this case, not inside it.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 peak reverses in FY2027: a 15-20% equity correction cuts AUC/A- and AUM-linked fees with a one-to-two-quarter lag, FX and securities-finance volumes fall from records, and Fed easing compresses NII, so revenue falls 3% against a sticky cost base and the pretax margin drops back to ~28%. Fee compression then holds growth to 2.5-3%, the transformation programme stalls at a 30% margin, the balance sheet consumes capital faster than revenue (1.1x retention, G-SIB surcharge creep), and the market exits at 12x FCFE. No solvency element - this is an earnings reset and de-rating, not a credit event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: State Street is a fee-led custody bank and asset manager that distributes ~80% of its earnings, so it is valued as a stream of free cash flow to equity (net income less the common equity retained to grow the balance sheet at a G-SIB CET1 level) capitalised at a 10.25% USD cost of equity, with deposits and wholesale funding treated as operating liabilities and only the ~$4.06B of preferred stock deducted ahead of common. FY0 is FY2026 built from nine months of actuals with Q4 held at the Q3 level (revenue +13.7%, ~32.8% pretax margin ex the Q1 repositioning charge); the 34-35% margins of Q2 and Q3 are not annualised. The three cases differ on whether 2026's market-driven revenue step holds, how much of the 35% pretax-margin target the transformation programme delivers, and how much capital balance-sheet growth absorbs.
key_risks_to_valuation: Market levels: ~60% of revenue (servicing and management fees) is ad-valorem on AUC/A and AUM; a 20% equity drawdown cuts fee revenue high-single-digits with a lag - the bear case's FY2027 -3%

Net interest income (~22% of revenue; 2,559 in 9M-2026, +19% year on year, NIM 1.12%) is the second swing factor: it reverses if the Fed eases faster than the forward curve, and deposits ($311.7B, up $37B in nine months) can leave as fast as they arrived
Margin execution: the base case takes the pretax margin to 33.5%, a level STT has reached in two quarters but not sustained for a year; each 1pp of terminal pretax margin is worth roughly $6/share
Capital: as a G-SIB, CET1 requirements, the G-SIB surcharge and any Basel III endgame re-proposal set the retention the model charges; the bear case lifts retention to 1.1x growth

Unmodelled: the pending Santander/CACEIS Latam acquisition (undisclosed terms, 2027 close). Preferred stock rose to $4.06B with the August 2026 Series L issue; a redemption of the $493M Series G would add ~$1.80/share back

The model holds the share count flat and treats buybacks as the FCFE distribution channel; per-share value is insensitive to repurchase pace but sensitive to the 10.25% cost of equity and the 21.5% tax rate (see sensitivity grid)

Quarterly visibility: Q3-2026 missed revenue consensus on other fee revenue and FX trading and the shares fell ~8% on the day despite an EPS beat; the model's FY0 does not depend on those lines recovering in Q4

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E total revenue, built from nine-month actuals (Q3-2026 10-Q: 9M total revenue 11,848 = fee revenue 9,288 + NII 2,559 + other; Q3 alone 4,004) plus a Q4 held at the Q3 level (~4,000). Total ~15,850, +13.7% on FY2025's 13,944 and +0.6% on the prior anchor of 15,750 (which implied a Q4 of 3,902). Q4 is NOT stepped up for seasonality or market levels (Q4-2025 was +3.4% on Q3-2025). No notable items in Q2 or Q3 2026; realised AFS gains/losses ~0. CROSS-CHECK against the guidance raised at Q3 (14 Oct 2026, per STT_Analysis.json): fee revenue +13-14% on FY2025's 10,980 and NII +15-16% on 2,960 give 15,810-15,970, midpoint ~15,880 (implied Q4 ~4,035). The 15,850 anchor sits inside the guided range, slightly under the midpoint, because management flagged other fee revenue (-29% sequentially) and FX trading (-14%) as volatile in Q3.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 10-Q cover-page common shares outstanding 272,078,043 at 2026-10-26 plus 5.1M dilutive awards (Q3-2026 diluted weighted average 279.292M less basic 274.182M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed inside noninterest expense (and therefore inside the pretax margin); buybacks ($1,200M FY2025; $1,200M in 9M-2026 at $400M/quarter, Q3 2.1M shares at an average $187.83) are the FCFE distribution channel, not a modelled count reduction. Q4-2026 repurchases after 26 October are not anticipated.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank convention (house precedent NTRS, NAB.AX, HBAN, GL): deposits ($311.7B at 2026-09-30), short-term borrowings and senior/subordinated long-term debt are operating funding of a deposit-taking custodian, serviced inside net interest income (FY2025 interest expense on long-term debt $1,230M is already netted in NII). FCFE is post-interest, so net debt is held at 0 and the flows are capitalised at the cost of equity. The only claim senior to common deducted is preferred stock (equity_bridge). Cash & due from banks and interest-bearing deposits at banks are operating assets funding client deposits, not surplus cash.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: net income ex-notables ~4,075 (pretax ~5,195 = 32.8% of 15,850: 9M pretax 3,746 + 89 Q1 repositioning + Q4 at ~34% of 4,000; 21.5% tax) x the ~71% payout actually realised in 9M-2026 (buybacks 1,200 + cash dividends paid 873 incl. preferred = 2,073 vs net income 2,938; a further 133 went to employee tax withholding on awards). reported_fcf is the CSV's FY2025 OCF-less-capex (11,898 - 1,055 = 10,843) and is deposit/trading-asset flow noise for a custody bank (FY2024 -14,136; 9M-2026 -13,509 on the same business); recorded for auditability only. The owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K equity-compensation note (STT_Annual_FY2025.txt:8927): compensation expense for deferred stock and performance awards $268M (FY2024 $223M, FY2023 $208M) plus $18M ($3M, $12M) of accelerated expense booked inside restructuring = $286M, 2.05% of FY2025 revenue. This replaces the prior ~2.0% ESTIMATE and confirms it; sbc_pct_path stays 2.0. Not tagged in XBRL since FY2018. It sits INSIDE noninterest expense, so it does not move the house value; sbc_pct_path is carried only so the engine's house/street memo band is computed. Separately, cash paid for employee tax withholding on awards was $106M FY2025 and $133M in 9M-2026 (financing activities) - a real cost of the plan in excess of the expense, not charged on this route.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS part of the business for a custody bank (NII 2,960 FY2025, ~21% of revenue). No cash is added back to value, so there is no double count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $1,200M + common dividends $909M + preferred dividends $226M = $2,335M returned vs $2,945M net income (79% total payout; management's medium-term target is ~80%). 9M-2026: buybacks $1,200M + cash dividends paid $873M (preferred $175M of it) vs net income $2,938M (71%). Quarterly dividend raised 10% to $0.92 from Q3-2026 ($3.68 annualised).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the FY2026 estimate (fiscal year closes 31 Dec 2026; nine months reported, Q4 held at the Q3 level, inside the range guided at Q3), so Y1 = FY2027. Last fully reported year is FY2025; latest filing is the Q3-2026 10-Q. FY2026 results and FY2027 guidance are due mid-January 2027 and should trigger a refresh that rolls FY0.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-10-26 (10-Q cover page); dilution from Q3-2026 weighted averages

balance_sheet_anchors.preferred_note: Read directly from the Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet and Table 34: Series G 493, I 1,481, J 842, K 743, L 496 = 4,055 carrying value at 2026-09-30 (3,559 at 2025-12-31). CORRECTION to the prior version: the August 2026 Series L issue ($500M, 6.35%) was assumed to refinance Series G one-for-one; it did not - Series G (redeemable since 2026-03-15, now fixed at 5.35% under the LIBOR Act) is still outstanding, so Series L is incremental. Preferred dividends 175 in 9M-2026 (59 in Q3); run-rate ~$265M/yr with Series L.
balance_sheet_anchors.roatce_fy0_est: FY2026E net income to common ~3,835 (4,075 less ~240 preferred dividends) / TCE 15,798 = ~24%, against a medium-term target of 'mid-20s'

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.25% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.2. Higher than NTRS's 9.75% (beta 1.1) because STT carries more market-sensitive revenue: SSGA management fees on $6.3T AUM, FX trading and securities finance (~13% of revenue) and a 52-week range of 104.64-195.93 that shows equity-like beta. Single rate across all three scenarios so risk is charged once, through the probability weights. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine's field name; no debt is in the capital structure being discounted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (premises, including the One Congress Boston HQ) are expensed inside noninterest expense (occupancy 487 FY2025) and therefore inside the pretax margin; no lease liability is added to net debt (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income is fully attributable to the parent.
inputs.engine_mapping: The component engine is driven as a bank P&L: 'EBITDA margin' = pretax-income margin + D&A % (7.0) + SBC % (2.0), so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = pretax income; cash_tax_rate 21.5% (FY2025 effective 21.1%, H1-2026 21.6%; FY2025 cash taxes paid 594 vs 786 book) turns that into net income before preferred dividends. da_pct and capex_pct share a 7.0% core (FY2025 capex 1,055 = 7.6% of revenue; depreciation is no longer tagged in XBRL - only the DIFFERENCE between the two paths matters on this route, plus the tax shield which nets to zero because D&A is inside EBITDA). The EXCESS of capex_pct over da_pct is the common equity retained to grow the balance sheet and RWA: retention = k x revenue growth, k = 0.8 base / 0.7 bull / 1.1 bear (TCE/revenue is ~1.0x; over FY2020-25 total equity grew 1.2%/yr while revenue grew 3.6%/yr on a ~80-110% payout, so most of STT's growth is ad-valorem fee growth on AUC/A that consumes little capital). Working-capital capture is 0. FCFE = net income - retained capital, capitalised at the cost of equity; preferred is deducted at carrying value in the bridge instead of its ~$232M dividend being charged to the flows. Acquired-intangible amortisation (223 FY2025, running off) is left inside the pretax margin uncredited - a deliberate conservatism worth ~$0.60/share/yr.
inputs.notes: MODEL (unchanged from 2026-10-02): Bank FCFE at cost of equity, through the component engine route - the routing table's bank row implemented as the house precedent for custody/trust banks (NTRS, NAB.AX, HBAN, GL): net_debt = 0, preferred deducted in equity_bridge, retention tied to growth. BVPS-compounding rejected because STT distributes 70-80% of earnings; owner-FCF DCF rejected because OCF swings from -13,210 (FY2024) to +11,898 (FY2025) on deposit and trading-asset flows. SBC: expensed (inside noninterest expense), share count held flat, funded by a real buyback programme. UPDATE 2026-11-19 for the Q3-2026 10-Q. ANCHORS REFRESHED: price; preferred 3,559 -> 4,055 (Series L incremental, not a refinancing - corrects a prior inference); diluted shares 279.6M -> 277.2M; balance sheet to 2026-09-30; SBC now read from the 10-K ($286M, was a $280M estimate). DRIVERS CHANGED: (1) base_revenue 15,750 -> 15,850 (9M actual 11,848 + Q4 at the Q3 level); (2) base case FY2027 pretax margin 31.5% -> 32.0% (ebitda_margin_path[0] 40.5 -> 41.0), because FY0 ex-notables is now tracking ~32.8% rather than 32.0% (Q2 34.3% and Q3 34.7% with no notable items; Q1 is seasonally low at ~27.9% ex the $89M repositioning charge) - the base case now gives back ~80bps in FY2027 instead of the 50bps originally intended, and would have given back 130bps had the path been left alone. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: all growth paths; base margins FY2028+ (32.5 -> 33.5%) - would move on a second year at or above 33% or a formal change to the ~35% medium-term target; bull and bear margin paths in full (bull FY2027 33.0% already sits above FY0; bear is a reset to FY2025's ex-notables level, which Q3 does not inform); retention coefficients 0.8/0.7/1.1 (CET1 fell 11.6% -> 11.0% in 9M on RWA normalisation while $2.1B was returned - consistent with, not contrary to, the base; would move on the March 2026 Basel proposals being finalised); tax 21.5% (Q3 21.5%, 9M 21.6%); cost of equity 10.25%; terminal growth and caps; weights 25/50/25. NOT MODELLED: the pending Santander/CACEIS Latam securities-services acquisition (terms undisclosed, close 2027; not mentioned in the Q3 10-Q). DATA FLAGS: (1) FY0 rests on nine months of actuals and is cross-checked to the Q3-raised guidance (fee revenue +13-14%, NII +15-16%, >500bps operating leverage), sitting just under the guided midpoint; (2) CSV EPS is basic (FY2025 9.55 vs diluted 9.40); (3) capex is running hot: purchases of premises and equipment 1,290 in 9M-2026 vs 788 in 9M-2025 - on this route capex is not a separate deduction (it reaches value through depreciation inside the pretax margin and through the retention charge), so watch for the depreciation step-up in FY2027 expenses.

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [28.0, 28.0, 28.5, 29.0, 29.5, 30.0, ...]: FY2027 revenue falls 3% (a 15-20% equity-market correction cuts ad-valorem servicing and SSGA fees, FX/securities-finance volumes fall from 2026 records, Fed easing compresses NII from the 1.13% Q2-26 NIM) against a sticky cost base, so the margin returns to FY2025's ex-notables ~28-29% and the transformation programme only reaches 30%.
bear.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 1.1 x revenue growth (balance sheet and RWA grow faster than revenue), floored at zero in FY2027 when revenue shrinks (no capital release assumed); terminal cap 12x FCFE reflects a de-rated custodian growing 2.5%.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin = EBITDA - SBC - D&A = [32.0, 32.5, 33.0, 33.5, 33.5, ...]: FY2027 gives back ~80bps from FY0's ~32.8% ex-notables as FX/securities-finance activity and NII normalise off the 2026 peak (FY2027 raised from 31.5% on 2026-11-19 after Q3 printed 34.7% with no notables), then the $1B transformation programme lifts it to 33.5% by FY2030 - most, not all, of management's ~35% medium-term target (STT has never sustained above ~30% reported on a full-year basis). FY2028+ unchanged.
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.8 x revenue growth = [3.6, 4.0, 4.0, 3.6, 3.6, 3.2, 3.2, 2.8, 2.4, 2.4]% of revenue, i.e. ~14-15% of net income in FY2027-28 (an ~85% payout, near management's ~80% target) falling to ~9% at the 3% terminal growth rate.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.25%/3.0% is 14.2x FCFE, under the 15x cap, so Gordon binds. 15x FCFE (~13.6x net income) is at the upper end of where custody banks have historically traded on earnings.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [33.0, 34.0, 35.0, 35.5, 35.5, ...]: the transformation programme delivers its full $1B run-rate by 2029, management's ~35% pretax target is hit on time and slightly exceeded.
bull.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.7 x revenue growth: Alpha software, ETF management fees and mandate wins are capital-light, so less CET1 is consumed per dollar of revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged at 25/50/25 (custody-bank precedent, NTRS). Bear held at 25% because the Analysis rates an equity/bond market correction as the single high-severity risk and FY2026 earnings are visibly lifted by record market levels and trading volumes (AUC/A +15%, AUM +16%, FX trading +24% year on year at nine months) - Q3 strengthened the earnings base and the peak-earnings concern in equal measure. Bull held at 25% because it needs the $1B transformation programme to fully land, markets to keep rising and NII to hold, all at once. Base at 50% is the reported run-rate with partial credit for the medium-term targets. The share price has fallen ~5% since the prior valuation while the estimate of value is slightly higher; that is not evidence for re-weighting.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
